newsitem.title: USA: Former Missouri House speaker indicted.
newsitem.headline: Former Missouri House speaker indicted.

text.p: The former speaker of the Missouri House was indicted Thursday by a special federal grand jury in Kansas City on charges of racketeering, bribery and mail fraud.

Bob Griffin, who retired from the legislature in January after serving as speaker for 15 years, was charged along with three individuals for their alleged involvement in "five schemes that involved the payment of bribes" to illegally influence the operation of the Missouri or Clay County governments, according to a news release from the U.S. Attorney's Office for the western district of Missouri.

One the "schemes" cited in the indictment involved a 1993 state highway bond bill. According to the U.S. Attorney, Griffin's alleged steering of a contract on behalf of several construction groups that supported the bond bill ended up with Griffin's son Jeff being hired for $5,000 to lobby on behalf of the bill.
Griffin denied any wrongdoing in comments he made to reporters Thursday outside the federal courthouse.

"The reason I'm here is because someone has lied to a grand jury. In a court of law, we'll find out who that is, and why. Whoever it is, I hope God forgives them, because I and my family never will," the former speaker said.
Chris Whitley, a spokesman for the U.S. Attorney, said Griffin and the others indicted were not required to enter pleas until their yet-to-be scheduled arraignments.
